overall_summary: Initial tests with romantic heartbreak and self-respect smartphone micro-habits saw modest views (under 50), but a recent experimental shift toward broader family and relationship emotional bonding (parents, spouses) dramatically outperformed baseline, hitting up to 1.4K views. Viewers resonate much more with warm, universal relationship bonds and soft family realism than niche heartbreak tropes.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on parents, spouses, and family care (e.g., 'पत्नी की यह बात हर पति को समझनी चाहिए' with 1451 views, 'आज किसी अपने को Call कर लेना' with 288 views) vastly outperformed romantic self-respect shorts.
winning_patterns.action: Pivot the core narrative focus toward universal relationship truths, subtle marital understanding, and family emotional bonds while keeping the 'Dil Ki Diary' intimate diary tone.

winning_patterns.evidence: Openings based on grounded everyday observations ('आज किसी अपने को Call कर लेना', wife/husband dynamics) drove higher engagement than overly dramatic digital/smartphone isolation hooks.
winning_patterns.action: Use subtle, grounded real-life everyday moments instead of digital device isolation as the starting point.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeatedly focusing on blocking numbers, deleting widgets, or clearing chat histories ('जब फोन के वॉलपेपर से उसकी पसंद की तस्वीर हटाई', 'Self Respect' status) consistently hovered between 0 to 41 views.
weak_patterns.action: Reduce hyper-niche digital breakup tropes; if discussing self-respect, tie it to broad life boundaries rather than just chat/phone deletions.
